summary: The refactor (resolveDelegatedAuthority extraction) and test coverage for expiry/revocation are solid, but wiring isDelegated() into decideApprovalStep() and decidePaymentEntry() turns a previously dormant schema gap into a live, exploitable broken-access-control vulnerability: POST /api/delegations (src/app/api/delegations/route.ts) requires only requireAuth() with zero role/rank check, and createDelegation()/validateDelegationInput() never verify that delegatorUserId actually held the authority (e.g. manager rank) for the scopeType/scopeId being handed away -- it only blocks delegateUserId === delegatorUserId (self-delegation to a specific user), not delegateRoleKey equal to the delegator's own role. Because decidePaymentEntry's decide route (src/app/api/erp/payment-entries/[id]/decide/route.ts) also only calls requireAuth() with no rank gate before canDecidePaymentEntry(), any authenticated low-rank ('member') user can now call POST /api/delegations once with scopeType 'approval_type', scopeId 'erp_payment_entry', delegateRoleKey: 'member' (or delegateUserId pointing at an accomplice account), and that grants payment-entry approval authority to themselves-by-role or an accomplice indefinitely -- completely bypassing the MANAGER_RANK mandatory-approval gate that erp-payment-entries-service.ts's own header says must never be skippable. The same gap applies to decideApprovalStep's generic approval-workflow fallback. The audit doc itself surfaces this exact gap in its closing note but self-contradicts ('no way to create a delegation that grants authority its creator didn't already need to have held' immediately followed by an acknowledgment that createDelegation does not verify this) and mischaracterizes it as an out-of-scope future-pass item rather than a live vulnerability this specific diff activates. This is a real financial-approval bypass, not a hypothetical, and should block merge until either createDelegation() verifies the delegator's own rank/authority for the scope at creation time, or isDelegated()'s consumption-time check is restricted to only trust delegations from a delegator who independently holds (or held) the required rank.
issues: Broken access control: POST /api/delegations (no role/rank check beyond requireAuth) lets any authenticated user create a delegation naming themselves via delegateRoleKey (or an accomplice via delegateUserId) as grantee for scopeType 'approval_type'/scopeId 'erp_payment_entry', which decidePaymentEntry's newly-wired hasDelegatedAuthority check will now honor -- a full bypass of the MANAGER_RANK mandatory-approval gate for real payment entries.

Same unguarded-delegation-creation gap applies to decideApprovalStep()'s new delegation fallback in approval-workflow-service.ts -- any rank-insufficient user can self-grant (via a role-keyed delegation) or accomplice-grant (via a user-keyed delegation) approval authority for any approval_type/entityType.

validateDelegationInput() blocks delegateUserId === delegatorUserId but does not block delegateRoleKey equal to the delegator's own role, so a single low-privilege user can grant their entire role cohort org-wide delegated authority in one API call.

Audit doc's closing note is self-contradictory: it claims 'no way to create a delegation that grants authority its creator didn't already need to have held' in the same sentence that admits createDelegation() doesn't verify this -- this understates a vulnerability this PR's own wiring makes live/exploitable rather than correctly flagging it as blocking.
